And.name: Andromeda
And.dek: Andromeda stretches away from Pegasus, with a great galaxy waiting beyond the naked-eye pattern.

Ant.name: Antlia
Ant.hed: A pump in the southern sky
Ant.dek: Antlia gives a scientific instrument a place among the southern constellations.

Aps.name: Apus
Aps.hed: A bird beyond the familiar sky
Aps.dek: Apus carries the bird-of-paradise into the far southern heavens.

Aql.name: Aquila
Aql.hed: An eagle on the Milky Way
Aql.dek: Altair anchors Aquila, a compact landmark along the bright river of our galaxy.

Aqr.name: Aquarius
Aqr.dek: Aquarius spreads the water-bearer’s pattern across a broad and often faint star field.

Ara.name: Ara
Ara.dek: Ara occupies a southern stretch of Milky Way below the curved body of Scorpius.

Ari.name: Aries
Ari.dek: Aries makes a modest pattern with a name far more familiar than its stars.

Aur.name: Auriga
Aur.dek: Capella draws the eye to Auriga and the rich Milky Way fields around it.

Boo.name: Boötes
Boo.dek: Arcturus gives Boötes a brilliant starting point for tracing its elongated figure.

CMa.name: Canis Major
CMa.dek: Sirius makes Canis Major unmistakable, while fainter stars complete the surrounding figure.

CMi.name: Canis Minor
CMi.hed: A small dog, a bright star
CMi.dek: Procyon is the conspicuous beacon of compact Canis Minor.

CVn.name: Canes Venatici
CVn.dek: Canes Venatici fills the quieter sky beneath the handle of the Big Dipper.

Cae.name: Caelum
Cae.hed: A chisel drawn in faint stars
Cae.dek: Caelum rewards a deliberate look at a small southern pattern.

Cam.name: Camelopardalis
Cam.dek: Camelopardalis fills a broad northern region with stars that require patient tracing.

Cap.name: Capricornus
Cap.dek: Capricornus forms a subtle pattern along the zodiac, best approached under a dark sky.

Car.name: Carina
Car.hed: The keel of a celestial ship
Car.dek: Canopus marks Carina, part of the old ship Argo’s enormous reach across the south.

Cas.name: Cassiopeia
Cas.dek: Cassiopeia’s zigzag provides an easy doorway into the northern Milky Way.

Cen.name: Centaurus
Cen.dek: Centaurus combines brilliant stars with a broad sweep of southern sky.

Cep.name: Cepheus
Cep.dek: Cepheus offers a quieter northern figure beside the more conspicuous Cassiopeia.

Cet.name: Cetus
Cet.hed: A sea monster with room to roam
Cet.dek: Cetus spreads across a large field south of the constellations of Pisces and Aries.

Cha.name: Chamaeleon
Cha.dek: Chamaeleon makes a small, faint figure deep in the southern sky.

Cir.name: Circinus
Cir.dek: Circinus places a compact geometric instrument beside the rich fields of Centaurus.

Cnc.name: Cancer
Cnc.dek: Cancer’s faint outline surrounds the Beehive, a cluster that rewards binocular exploration.

Col.name: Columba
Col.dek: Columba lies south of Canis Major and Lepus, away from the brightest familiar patterns.

Com.name: Coma Berenices
Com.hed: A queen’s hair, a scattering of stars
Com.dek: Coma Berenices invites a wide-field look at a loose gathering between Leo and Boötes.

CrA.name: Corona Australis
CrA.dek: Corona Australis makes a small curved figure near Sagittarius.

CrB.name: Corona Borealis
CrB.hed: A crown with an open edge
CrB.dek: Corona Borealis draws a compact arc between Boötes and Hercules.

Crt.name: Crater
Crt.hed: A cup upon the Water Snake
Crt.dek: Crater is a faint companion to the long figure of Hydra.

Cru.name: Crux
Cru.dek: Crux packs a striking landmark into a small constellation against the Milky Way.

Crv.name: Corvus
Crv.dek: Corvus makes a readily traced quadrilateral near Virgo and Hydra.

Cyg.name: Cygnus
Cyg.dek: Deneb anchors Cygnus, whose long cross reaches through a rich Milky Way field.

Del.name: Delphinus
Del.dek: Delphinus makes a compact diamond-and-tail pattern near Aquila.

Dor.name: Dorado
Dor.hed: A fish in the deep south
Dor.dek: Dorado gives a southern fish a place in a field shared with the Large Magellanic Cloud.

Dra.name: Draco
Dra.dek: Draco threads a long, bending figure between the two Bears.

Equ.name: Equuleus
Equ.dek: Equuleus is a small and understated neighbor of the much larger winged horse.

Eri.name: Eridanus
Eri.dek: Eridanus winds from the neighborhood of Orion toward the far southern sky.

For.name: Fornax
For.hed: A furnace in a quiet field
For.dek: Fornax gives a scientific instrument a faint southern outline.

Gem.name: Gemini
Gem.dek: Castor and Pollux guide the eye into the paired figures of Gemini.

Gru.name: Grus
Gru.hed: A crane in the southern sky
Gru.dek: Grus offers a long-necked bird pattern south of the watery constellations.

Her.name: Hercules
Her.hed: The hero beyond the bright stars
Her.dek: Hercules takes shape around the Keystone, a useful starting point in a large constellation.

Hor.name: Horologium
Hor.dek: Horologium is a faint southern pattern named for a timekeeping instrument.

Hya.name: Hydra
Hya.dek: Hydra stretches beneath several constellations, rewarding a chart-wide view.

Hyi.name: Hydrus
Hyi.dek: Hydrus is a separate southern figure, distinct from the much larger Hydra.

Ind.name: Indus
Ind.hed: A human figure in the southern sky
Ind.dek: Indus preserves a historical European constellation name in a faint southern field.

LMi.name: Leo Minor
LMi.hed: A little lion between larger neighbors
LMi.dek: Leo Minor occupies the quieter sky between Leo and Ursa Major.

Lac.name: Lacerta
Lac.hed: A lizard in the Milky Way
Lac.dek: Lacerta is a small zigzag between the more conspicuous Cygnus and Cassiopeia.

Leo.name: Leo
Leo.hed: A lion written in bright stars
Leo.dek: The Sickle and the Lion’s hindquarters give Leo a particularly readable outline.

Lep.name: Lepus
Lep.dek: Lepus makes a separate figure immediately south of Orion.

Lib.name: Libra
Lib.dek: Libra’s stars occupy the space between Virgo and Scorpius.

Lup.name: Lupus
Lup.dek: Lupus fills a southern field between Centaurus and Scorpius.

Lyn.name: Lynx
Lyn.dek: Lynx runs through a faint northern field between brighter, more familiar figures.

Lyr.name: Lyra
Lyr.hed: A small lyre with a brilliant voice
Lyr.dek: Vega makes Lyra easy to locate; the smaller pattern takes a closer look.

Men.name: Mensa
Men.hed: A mountain carried into the sky
Men.dek: Mensa has no stick figure in this atlas; its constellation card keeps its identity visible.

Mic.name: Microscopium
Mic.hed: A microscope without a stick figure
Mic.dek: Microscopium has no stick figure in this atlas; its card belongs in the full constellation collection.

Mon.name: Monoceros
Mon.dek: Monoceros fills the Milky Way between Orion and the two Dogs.

Mus.name: Musca
Mus.dek: Musca occupies a small southern field just south of Crux.

Nor.name: Norma
Nor.hed: A tool among the Milky Way stars
Nor.dek: Norma places a faint instrument-shaped constellation in a rich southern region.

Oct.name: Octans
Oct.dek: Octans contains the south celestial pole in a field without a brilliant pole star.

Oph.name: Ophiuchus
Oph.dek: Ophiuchus stands between the head and tail regions of Serpens.

Ori.name: Orion
Ori.dek: Belt, sword, shoulders, and feet make Orion a rewarding portrait to explore layer by layer.

Pav.name: Pavo
Pav.hed: A peacock in the southern heavens
Pav.dek: Pavo spreads a southern bird figure beyond the most familiar northern landmarks.

Peg.name: Pegasus
Peg.hed: The horse beyond the Great Square
Peg.dek: Pegasus extends away from a large square that helps organize the surrounding sky.

Per.name: Perseus
Per.hed: A hero in a crowded star field
Per.dek: Perseus lies along the northern Milky Way between Andromeda and Auriga.

Phe.name: Phoenix
Phe.dek: Phoenix marks a southern bird figure between brighter landmarks in neighboring constellations.

Pic.name: Pictor
Pic.dek: Pictor occupies a faint southern field near Carina’s brilliant beacon.

PsA.name: Piscis Austrinus
PsA.hed: One fish beneath the Water Bearer
PsA.dek: Fomalhaut gives Piscis Austrinus a bright reference point in a relatively quiet field.

Psc.name: Pisces
Psc.hed: Two fish linked across the sky
Psc.dek: Pisces stretches a long, faint pattern around the neighborhood of Pegasus.

Pup.name: Puppis
Pup.hed: The stern of the great ship
Pup.dek: Puppis preserves another portion of Argo amid rich southern Milky Way fields.

Pyx.name: Pyxis
Pyx.hed: A compass for a celestial voyage
Pyx.dek: Pyxis is a small southern constellation beside the old ship’s larger parts.

Ret.name: Reticulum
Ret.hed: A measuring grid among the stars
Ret.dek: Reticulum gives an observing instrument a compact southern home.

Scl.name: Sculptor
Scl.hed: A workshop in the southern sky
Scl.dek: Sculptor occupies a broad, faint field south of Cetus.

Sco.name: Scorpius
Sco.dek: Antares and a curving tail make Scorpius one of the sky’s most expressive figures.

Sct.name: Scutum
Sct.hed: A shield against the Milky Way
Sct.dek: Scutum is small, but its setting places it among rich galactic star fields.

Ser.name: Serpens
Ser.dek: Serpens Caput and Serpens Cauda lie on opposite sides of Ophiuchus and share one constellation identity.

Sex.name: Sextans
Sex.dek: Sextans is a faint equatorial figure south of Leo.

Sge.name: Sagitta
Sge.hed: An arrow in a rich field
Sge.dek: Sagitta makes a small, distinctive figure between Aquila and Vulpecula.

Sgr.name: Sagittarius
Sgr.dek: Sagittarius combines a familiar asterism with the rich direction toward the galaxy’s center.

Tau.name: Taurus
Tau.dek: Aldebaran, the Hyades, and the Pleiades provide several ways into Taurus.

Tel.name: Telescopium
Tel.dek: Telescopium is a faint instrument constellation south of Sagittarius.

TrA.name: Triangulum Australe
TrA.dek: Triangulum Australe forms a compact geometric landmark in the southern sky.

Tri.name: Triangulum
Tri.hed: Three stars make a northern triangle
Tri.dek: Triangulum offers a small, simple figure near Andromeda and Aries.

Tuc.name: Tucana
Tuc.dek: Tucana shares its far southern field with the Small Magellanic Cloud.

UMa.name: Ursa Major
UMa.hed: The Great Bear beyond the Dipper
UMa.dek: The Big Dipper is the familiar starting point; Ursa Major reaches much farther.

UMi.name: Ursa Minor
UMi.dek: Polaris anchors the end of Ursa Minor’s handle, while fainter stars complete the Little Dipper.

Vel.name: Vela
Vel.dek: Vela preserves the sails of Argo in a broad and richly populated southern field.

Vir.name: Virgo
Vir.dek: Spica gives Virgo a bright landmark within a large equatorial constellation.

Vol.name: Volans
Vol.dek: Volans is a small southern pattern named for a flying fish.

Vul.name: Vulpecula
Vul.dek: Vulpecula occupies a faint Milky Way field between Cygnus and Sagitta.
